# Stage-3 proof: Baffet-type 2D energy for a matched Maxwell-Debye PML

Problem id: `2d_maxwell_pml_energy_functional_exploration`

Task: `task-stage3-final-report`

## Purpose

The previous stage-3 artifact proves that the standard stretched-coordinate
Maxwell-Debye PML is perfectly matched, but only gives a monotone energy in the
one-dimensional normal-incidence block.  This artifact records a full two
dimensional constant-coefficient Baffet-type formulation for the same stretched
coordinate model.  The formulation uses a time primitive of the electric field
and a time primitive of the Debye polarization, which is exactly the type of
augmented/time-integrated variable used in Baffet-type PML energy arguments.

## Assumptions and notation

Let
\[
e=\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty>0,\quad \mu>0,\quad \chi>0,\quad \tau>0.
\]
In the Laplace domain,
\[
\varepsilon_D(s)=e+\frac{\chi}{1+\tau s}.
\]
On one constant-coefficient PML block let
\[
\sigma_x,\sigma_y\ge 0,\qquad
a=\sigma_x+\sigma_y,\qquad b=\sigma_x\sigma_y,
\]
and assume \(a>0\) for the PML block.  The undamped physical block \(a=b=0\)
uses the ordinary Maxwell-Debye energy and is coupled by the usual transmission
flux.  Define
\[
\Gamma_1=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_x&0\\0&\sigma_y\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\Gamma_2=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_y-\sigma_x&0\\0&\sigma_x-\sigma_y\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For a vector \(v\), write \(|v|_M^2=v\cdot Mv\).

Let \(u\) be the time primitive of the electric field:
\[
E=u_t.
\]
Let \(q\) be the time primitive of the Debye polarization:
\[
q_t=P.
\]
The Debye law is written in compatible primitive form
\[
\tau P_t+P=\chi u_t,\qquad q+\tau P=\chi u.
\]
The second relation is preserved by the first two equations if it is true at
initial time.

## Baffet-type matched PML system

Introduce the Baffet auxiliary vector \(\phi=(\phi_x,\phi_y)\) and
\[
\lambda=\nabla u+\phi.
\]
The constant-coefficient two-dimensional repaired model is
\[
\boxed{
\mu\{e(u_{tt}+a u_t+b u)+P_t+aP+bq\}-\nabla\cdot\lambda=0,}
\tag{1}
\]
\[
\boxed{\phi_t+\Gamma_1\phi=\Gamma_2\nabla u,}
\tag{2}
\]
\[
\boxed{\tau P_t+P=\chi u_t,\qquad q_t=P,\qquad q+\tau P=\chi u.}
\tag{3}
\]
Outer boundary conditions are taken so that the boundary flux
\[
\int_{\partial\Omega}(u_t+au)\lambda\cdot n\,ds
\]
is zero or nonpositive.  For a PEC outer boundary, the compatible primitive
condition is \(u=0\), hence \(u_t=E=0\), on that boundary.  On piecewise
constant internal interfaces, the usual transmission conditions are continuity
of \(u\) and \(\lambda\cdot n\), so the flux cancels pairwise.

## Equivalence with the stretched-coordinate Maxwell-Debye PML

For constant coefficients, Laplace transforming (2) gives
\[
\widehat\phi_x=\frac{\sigma_y-\sigma_x}{s+\sigma_x}\partial_x\widehat u,
\qquad
\widehat\phi_y=\frac{\sigma_x-\sigma_y}{s+\sigma_y}\partial_y\widehat u.
\]
Thus
\[
\widehat\lambda_x
=\frac{s+\sigma_y}{s+\sigma_x}\partial_x\widehat u
=\frac{S_y}{S_x}\partial_x\widehat u,\qquad
\widehat\lambda_y
=\frac{s+\sigma_x}{s+\sigma_y}\partial_y\widehat u
=\frac{S_x}{S_y}\partial_y\widehat u,
\]
where
\[
S_i(s)=1+\frac{\sigma_i}{s}=\frac{s+\sigma_i}{s}.
\]
The Debye compatibility gives
\[
\widehat P=\frac{\chi s}{1+\tau s}\widehat u,\qquad
\widehat q=\frac{1}{s}\widehat P.
\]
Therefore
\[
e(s^2+as+b)\widehat u+s\widehat P+a\widehat P+b\widehat q
=\left(e+\frac{\chi}{1+\tau s}\right)(s^2+as+b)\widehat u
=\varepsilon_D(s)s^2S_xS_y\widehat u.
\]
Equation (1) becomes
\[
\mu\varepsilon_D(s)s^2S_xS_y\widehat u
=\nabla\cdot\widehat\lambda.
\]
Dividing by \(S_xS_y\) gives
\[
\mu\varepsilon_D(s)s^2\widehat u
=S_x^{-1}\partial_x(S_x^{-1}\partial_x\widehat u)
+S_y^{-1}\partial_y(S_y^{-1}\partial_y\widehat u).
\]
Since \(\widehat E=s\widehat u\), this is exactly the second-order equation
obtained by eliminating \(H_x,H_y\) from the standard stretched-coordinate
Maxwell-Debye PML while keeping
\[
(1+\tau s)\widehat P=\chi \widehat E.
\]
Consequently this Baffet-type time-domain system has the same planar-interface
perfect matching as the standard stretched-coordinate PML: at an \(x\)-interface
with \(S_y=1\), the normal symbol satisfies \(\nu=S_x\nu_0\) and the tangential
Maxwell admittance is unchanged.

## Energy functional

Define
\[
\alpha=1+2a\tau,\qquad
\beta=a+b\tau,\qquad
\gamma=a^2+b(1+a\tau).
\]
The Baffet-Debye energy is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_{BD}
=\frac12\int_\Omega \{&
\mu e(u_t+a u)^2+|\lambda|^2
+|\phi|_{a^{-1}\Gamma_1}^2+\mu e\,b u^2\\
&+\frac{\mu}{\chi}\left(\alpha P^2+2\beta Pq+\gamma q^2\right)
\}\,dxdy .
\end{aligned}}
\tag{4}
\]
The \(P,q\) block is positive definite whenever \(a>0\).  Indeed
\[
\alpha>0,\qquad
\alpha\gamma-\beta^2
=b+ab\tau+2a^3\tau+b(2a^2-b)\tau^2>0,
\]
because \(a=\sigma_x+\sigma_y>0\), \(b=\sigma_x\sigma_y\ge0\), \(\tau>0\), and
\(2a^2-b\ge0\).  Thus (4) is nonnegative, and it is coercive on the PML block
modulo the usual zero modes of the primitive variables and boundary conditions.

## Energy identity

Test (1) with \(u_t+a u\).  The nondispersive part gives the usual Baffet
calculation:
\[
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\int_\Omega
\mu e\{(u_t+a u)^2+b u^2\}\,dxdy
+\int_\Omega \mu e\,ab u^2\,dxdy
=\int_\Omega (u_t+a u)\nabla\cdot\lambda\,dxdy
-\mu\int_\Omega (P_t+aP+bq)(u_t+a u)\,dxdy .
\tag{5}
\]
The boundary part of the first term is the flux stated above, and the interior
part is handled by the same Baffet multiplier used for \(\lambda\).  Specifically,
from
\[
\lambda_t+\Gamma_1\lambda=\nabla u_t+\widetilde\Gamma_2\nabla u,\qquad
\widetilde\Gamma_2=\Gamma_2+\Gamma_1
=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_y&0\\0&\sigma_x\end{pmatrix},
\]
and the multiplier
\[
g=(I+a^{-1}\Gamma_1)\lambda-a^{-1}\Gamma_1\nabla u,
\]
one obtains
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\int_\Omega
\left(|\lambda|^2+|\phi|_{a^{-1}\Gamma_1}^2\right)\,dxdy\\
&\quad+\int_\Omega
\left(|\lambda|^2_{\Gamma_1(I+a^{-1}\Gamma_1)}
+\frac{b}{a}|\nabla u|^2\right)\,dxdy
=\int_\Omega \nabla(u_t+a u)\cdot\lambda\,dxdy .
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
This is the two-dimensional Baffet identity; it uses
\(\Gamma_1\widetilde\Gamma_2=bI\) and
\(a^{-1}\Gamma_1(\Gamma_1+\widetilde\Gamma_2)+\widetilde\Gamma_2=aI\).

It remains to compute the Debye primitive contribution.  Using
\[
u_t+a u
=\frac{\tau P_t+(1+a\tau)P+a q}{\chi},
\]
we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(P_t+aP+bq)(u_t+a u)\\
&=\frac1\chi\Big[
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}
\left(\alpha P^2+2\beta Pq+\gamma q^2\right)
+\tau P_t^2+\tau(a^2-b)P^2+abq^2
\Big].
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Here \(q_t=P\), and the constants \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) are exactly those in
(4).

Adding (5), (6), and (7) gives the full identity
\[
\boxed{
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{BD}(t)
=-\mathcal D_{BD}(t)
+\int_{\partial\Omega}(u_t+a u)\lambda\cdot n\,ds,}
\tag{8}
\]
where
\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal D_{BD}
=\int_\Omega \{&
|\lambda|^2_{\Gamma_1(I+a^{-1}\Gamma_1)}
+\frac{b}{a}|\nabla u|^2+\mu e\,ab u^2\\
&+\frac{\mu}{\chi}\left[
\tau P_t^2+\tau(a^2-b)P^2+abq^2
\right]\}\,dxdy .
\end{aligned}}
\tag{9}
\]
All displayed terms in \(\mathcal D_{BD}\) are nonnegative for
\(\sigma_x,\sigma_y\ge0\), \(a>0\), and positive material parameters.  Under PEC
or canceling transmission flux, (8) gives
\[
\mathcal E_{BD}(t)+\int_0^t\mathcal D_{BD}(r)\,dr\le \mathcal E_{BD}(0).
\]

## Classification and nullspace

This is a full two-dimensional constant-coefficient dissipative identity for an
exact stretched-coordinate Maxwell-Debye PML, written in Baffet-type
time-integrated variables.  It is non-increasing, not strictly decreasing on the
whole computational domain.  The nullspace contains the already identified
undamped physical-region stationary magnetic modes; in the PML block, the
dissipation also leaves the standard primitive-variable gauge modes unless fixed
by boundary/transmission compatibility.  Thus the sharp statement is
non-increase plus a characterized nullspace/no-abnormal-growth estimate, not
strict decay of every nonzero whole-domain state.

For spatially varying damping profiles, this artifact does not claim an energy
identity.  As in the Baffet reference, the verified scope is constant
coefficients, and piecewise constant layers are handled blockwise with
transmission flux cancellation.

# Stage-3 proof: repaired PML candidates and dissipative-energy classification

Problem id: `2d_maxwell_pml_energy_functional_exploration`

Task: `task-stage3-repaired-model-energy`

## Input fact from the matching test

The v2 covariantly damped Maxwell--Debye model has the verified stage-2 monotone
energy identity, but the stage-3 interface calculation shows that it is not a
perfectly matched layer.  In an \(x\)-layer with \(\rho_x=\rho>0,\rho_y=0\),
\[
Y_{v2}^2-Y_0^2
=-\frac{\rho}{\mu^2}\left[
\frac{\mu\chi\tau}{(1+\tau s)(1+\tau(s+\rho))}
+\frac{k_y^2}{s^2(s+\rho)}
\right],
\]
so the v2 reflection coefficient is not identically zero.

Therefore a repaired model must keep the physical Debye law as a function of the
Laplace variable \(s\), not \(s+\rho\), and must implement damping through
coordinate stretching or an equivalent split/ADE system.

## Candidate 1: classical stretched-coordinate Maxwell--Debye PML

Let
\[
\varepsilon_D(s)=\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty+\frac{\chi}{1+\tau s},
\qquad
S_i(s)=1+\frac{\sigma_i}{s},\quad i=x,y.
\]
In the physical region \(\sigma_x=\sigma_y=0\).  In the PML the coefficients are
nonnegative and are first analyzed as piecewise constant near each planar
interface.

The Laplace-domain repaired model is
\[
\boxed{
s\varepsilon_D(s)\widehat E
=S_x^{-1}\partial_x\widehat H_y
-S_y^{-1}\partial_y\widehat H_x,}
\]
\[
\boxed{
\mu s\widehat H_x=-S_y^{-1}\partial_y\widehat E,\qquad
\mu s\widehat H_y=S_x^{-1}\partial_x\widehat E,}
\]
\[
\boxed{(1+\tau s)\widehat P=\chi\widehat E.}
\]
Equivalently, the Debye law is not damped:
\[
P+\tau P_t=\chi E.
\]

### Perfect matching

At an \(x\)-interface, \(S_y=1\).  With tangential Fourier number \(k_y\),
the physical normal symbol satisfies
\[
\nu_0^2=k_y^2+\mu s^2\varepsilon_D(s),\qquad
Y_0=\frac{\nu_0}{\mu s}.
\]
In the PML,
\[
s\varepsilon_D E=S_x^{-1}\nu H_y-ik_yH_x,\qquad
\mu sH_x=-ik_yE,\qquad
\mu sH_y=S_x^{-1}\nu E.
\]
The dispersion relation gives
\[
\left(S_x^{-1}\nu\right)^2=k_y^2+\mu s^2\varepsilon_D(s),
\]
hence \(\nu=S_x\nu_0\) and
\[
Y_+=\frac{S_x^{-1}\nu}{\mu s}=\frac{\nu_0}{\mu s}=Y_0.
\]
Thus the planar-interface reflection coefficient is \(R=0\) for every
\((s,k_y)\) in the Laplace half-plane.  The same argument applies to a
\(y\)-interface with \(x,y\) interchanged.

### Time-domain ADE realization

Define the causal operator
\[
\mathcal A_i=S_i^{-1}=\frac{s}{s+\sigma_i}
\]
in the Laplace domain.  Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal A_i f=f+\psi_i,\qquad
(\partial_t+\sigma_i)\psi_i=-\sigma_i f.
\]
Then a time-domain unsplit ADE form is
\[
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E_t+P_t
=\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x
+\psi_{E,x}-\psi_{E,y},
\]
\[
\mu H_{x,t}=-\partial_yE-\psi_{H_x,y},\qquad
\mu H_{y,t}=\partial_xE+\psi_{H_y,x},
\]
\[
P+\tau P_t=\chi E,
\]
with
\[
(\partial_t+\sigma_x)\psi_{E,x}=-\sigma_x\partial_xH_y,\qquad
(\partial_t+\sigma_y)\psi_{E,y}=-\sigma_y\partial_yH_x,
\]
\[
(\partial_t+\sigma_y)\psi_{H_x,y}=-\sigma_y\partial_yE,\qquad
(\partial_t+\sigma_x)\psi_{H_y,x}=-\sigma_x\partial_xE.
\]
Interface conditions are continuity of the physical tangential traces.  For an
\(x\)-interface these are \(E\) and \(H_y\).  The auxiliary variables vanish in the
physical region and are initialized consistently with the causal convolution.

### Naive energy calculation

The natural physical Debye energy is
\[
\mathcal E_{\rm phys}
=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2+\chi^{-1}P^2\right)\,dxdy.
\]
It is positive because
\(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_\infty,\mu,\chi>0\).  Using
\[
E P_t=\frac{1}{2\chi}\partial_t(P^2)+\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2
\]
and the PEC boundary condition \(E=0\) on the outer boundary gives
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{\rm phys}
=-\int_\Omega\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2\,dxdy
+\int_\Omega
\left[
E(\psi_{E,x}-\psi_{E,y})
-H_x\psi_{H_x,y}
+H_y\psi_{H_y,x}
\right]\,dxdy .
\]
The Maxwell principal part contributes only the boundary flux
\[
\int_{\partial\Omega}E(H_y n_x-H_x n_y)\,ds,
\]
which vanishes under PEC at the outer boundary and cancels by transmission at
internal material/PML interfaces when the tangential traces are continuous.

The remaining auxiliary terms are not sign-definite in this naive energy.
Therefore the positive physical Debye energy alone is not a monotone energy for
the exact stretched-coordinate PML.

### Classification

This candidate is the formula-level perfect-matching repair.  A local monotone
energy for the full 2D Maxwell--Debye ADE system is not certified here.  The
calculation above identifies the exact terms that a Baffet-type augmented energy
would have to absorb:
\[
E\psi_{E,x},\quad E\psi_{E,y},\quad
H_x\psi_{H_x,y},\quad H_y\psi_{H_y,x}.
\]
The literature record supports that such augmented energies are non-naive and
that constant-coefficient damping is the natural first scope for a sharp identity.

### Reduced normal-incidence 1D energy identity

There is one important positive result for the exact stretched-coordinate model.
In the \(x\)-layer normal-incidence block \(k_y=0\), the standard stretch gives
\[
(\partial_t+\rho)(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E+P)=\partial_xH_y,
\qquad
\mu(\partial_t+\rho)H_y=\partial_xE,
\]
\[
P+\tau P_t=\chi E.
\]
This is exactly the \(k_y=0\) restriction of the perfectly matched stretched
model, not the v2 model, because the Debye law still uses \(\partial_t\) rather
than \(\partial_t+\rho\).

Multiply the first equation by \(E\), the second by \(H_y\), and use
\[
E=\frac{P+\tau P_t}{\chi}.
\]
Then
\[
E P_t=\frac{1}{2\chi}\partial_t(P^2)+\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2,
\]
and
\[
\rho E P
=\frac{\rho}{\chi}P^2+\frac{\rho\tau}{2\chi}\partial_t(P^2).
\]
After integrating by parts, the principal terms give only the boundary flux
\(\int_{\partial I}EH_y n_x\,ds\).  Hence
\[
\boxed{
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_{1d,sc}
=-\int_I\left(
\rho\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu\rho H_y^2
+\frac{\rho}{\chi}P^2+\frac{\tau}{\chi}P_t^2
\right)\,dx
+\int_{\partial I}EH_y n_x\,ds,}
\]
where
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal E_{1d,sc}
=\frac12\int_I\left(
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_y^2
+\frac{1+\rho\tau}{\chi}P^2
\right)\,dx.}
\]
This energy is positive for \(\rho,\tau,\chi>0\), and it is dissipative under
PEC or otherwise nonpositive boundary flux.  It explains why the v2 idea is
close to a useful construction in normal incidence, but it does not solve the
full 2D oblique problem: as soon as \(k_y\ne0\), the exact stretched model
contains the ADE memory couplings displayed above.

## Candidate 2: generalized CFS/ADE stretched-coordinate PML

Let
\[
S_i(s)=\kappa_i+\frac{\sigma_i}{s+\alpha_i},
\qquad
\kappa_i\ge1,\quad \sigma_i\ge0,\quad \alpha_i\ge0.
\]
The repaired Laplace-domain equations are the same as Candidate 1, with these
\(S_i\).  In particular the Debye law remains
\[
(1+\tau s)\widehat P=\chi\widehat E.
\]

For a planar \(x\)-interface with \(S_y=1\), the same calculation gives
\[
\nu=S_x\nu_0,\qquad Y_+=Y_0,
\]
so the continuous model is perfectly matched whenever the stretch is applied to
the spatial derivatives and the physical material law is left unchanged.

If \(S_i^{-1}\) is rational with poles in \(\Re s<0\), it can be implemented by
ADE variables.  The CFS shift \(\alpha_i>0\) is a standard way to improve
low-frequency/evanescent and late-time behavior, but a monotone time-domain
energy requires an explicit positive realization of the memory kernel.  No such
positive memory theorem is claimed here for the full 2D Maxwell--Debye system.

Classification: perfectly matched at the continuous planar-interface level;
recommended if long-time CFS behavior is needed; energy status is boundedness or
passive-memory proof pending, not a completed monotone identity.

## Candidate 3: MPML-type extra damping

An MPML-type repair adds damping in more than the normal coordinate direction.
For example, in an \(x\)-layer one may replace a scalar stretch by a multiaxial
stretch depending also on tangential damping parameters.  This is useful for
removing long-time instabilities or Jordan-block behavior in some systems.

However, if the tangential stretch is nontrivial at the physical/PML interface,
the planar admittance generally changes.  The MPML literature inspected for this
run explicitly treats MPML as a stability-oriented absorbing layer and records
that exact perfect matching may be lost in multiaxial variants.

Classification: absorbing/stability repair, not the primary exact-matching
repair for the present Maxwell--Debye interface theorem.

## Complete dissipative identity that is currently verified

The only complete positive monotone identity verified in the existing Iteris
memory is for the v2 covariantly damped absorbing layer:
\[
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty D_\rho E
=\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x-D_\rho P,
\]
\[
\mu(\partial_t+\rho_y)H_x=-\partial_yE,\qquad
\mu(\partial_t+\rho_x)H_y=\partial_xE,
\]
\[
P+\tau D_\rho P=\chi E,\qquad D_\rho=\partial_t+\rho_x+\rho_y.
\]
Its energy is
\[
\mathcal E_\rho(t)=\frac12\int_\Omega
\left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2+\chi^{-1}P^2\right)\,dxdy
\]
and the verified identity is
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal E_\rho(t)
=-\int_\Omega\left(
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty\rho E^2
+\mu\rho_yH_x^2
+\mu\rho_xH_y^2
+\frac{\rho}{\chi}P^2
+\frac{\tau}{\chi}|D_\rho P|^2
\right)\,dxdy.
\]
This identity is genuinely dissipative, but the model is not perfectly matched.
It should therefore be described as a stable absorbing-layer model, not as a
standard PML.

## Formula-level obstruction to strict decay on the whole domain

Even for a perfectly matched repair, strict decay of a total energy controlling
all fields on the whole computational domain cannot hold without a nullspace.
Assume a physical subregion where \(\sigma_x=\sigma_y=0\) and choose
\[
E=0,\qquad P=0,\qquad H_x=\partial_x\phi,\qquad H_y=\partial_y\phi,
\]
with \(\phi\) smooth and compactly supported inside that undamped physical
subregion.  Then
\[
\partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x=0,\qquad
\partial_yE=\partial_xE=0,
\]
and all PML auxiliary variables initialized at zero remain zero for at least this
exact stationary solution.  The magnetic energy is positive if \(\nabla\phi\ne0\),
but every damping term in the PML vanishes.

## statement

For Maxwell-Debye with A(s)=epsilon0 epsilon_infty+chi/(1+tau s), the standard stretched-coordinate PML keeps A(s) and replaces partial_i by S_i(s)^{-1} partial_i, S_i=1+sigma_i/s.  At a planar x-interface with S_x=(s+rho)/s, S_y=1, the transmitted normal number is kappa_sc=S_x kappa_0 and the admittance is Y_sc=-kappa_sc/(mu s S_x)=-kappa_0/(mu s), hence the reflection coefficient is zero for every outgoing physical mode.  In the one-dimensional x-PML normal-incidence block, the exact stretched system (partial_t+rho)(epsilon0 epsilon_infty E+P)=partial_x H_y, mu(partial_t+rho)H_y=partial_xE, P+tau P_t=chi E has the positive energy integral 1/2 int (epsilon0 epsilon_infty E^2+mu H_y^2+(1+rho tau)chi^{-1}P^2) dx and derivative -int (rho epsilon0 epsilon_infty E^2+mu rho H_y^2+rho chi^{-1}P^2+tau chi^{-1}P_t^2) dx, up to the usual boundary flux.  Full derivation and full 2D classification: artifacts/proofs/stage3_repaired_model_energy.md.

\title{Problem Sheet for Iteris: Energy Functionals for 2D Maxwell--PML}
\author{Prepared source problem}
\date{\today}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
This note is a self-contained source problem for an Iteris run.  The system to be analyzed is the two-dimensional TM Maxwell--PML model with polarization \(P\), PML auxiliary variables \(P_{z,1},P_{z,2},Q_x,Q_y\), and perfectly conducting boundary condition.  The first target is to find a genuinely monotone decreasing energy functional in two space dimensions.  If such a monotone energy cannot be found, the fallback target is to find a positive energy functional that proves boundedness/no abnormal long-time growth, in the same spirit as the long-time-stability role of MPML.  The non-fractional case should be understood as the special case \(\alpha=1\) of the displayed polarization law.
\end{abstract}

\section{Primary Goal}

Let \(\Om\subset\R^2\) be a rectangular computational domain containing a physical region and a PML layer.  The absorption parameters are
\[
  \sx=\sx(x)\ge0,\qquad \sy=\sy(y)\ge0,
\]
or, in a harder variant,
\[
  \sx=\sx(x,y)\ge0,\qquad \sy=\sy(x,y)\ge0.
\]
The main goal is to analyze the two-dimensional system in Section~\ref{sec:model} and construct an energy functional \(\Ecal(t)\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Strong target: monotone decreasing energy.}
Find a positive energy functional such that
\[
  \frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Ecal(t)=-\Dcal(t)\le0.
\]
This is the preferred outcome.
\item \textbf{Fallback target: bounded/non-growing energy.}
If no monotone energy can be found, find a positive energy functional that rules out abnormal growth from the PML layer, for example
\[
  \Ecal(t)\le C\,\Ecal(0)
\]
with \(C\) independent of long time if possible.  If only a Gronwall estimate
\[
  \frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Ecal(t)\le C_\sigma\Ecal(t)
\]
is available, identify the precise terms responsible for the possible growth and whether they are coefficient-gradient terms, corner-PML terms, or algebraic sign-indefinite terms.
\item \textbf{Useful obstruction.}
If the strong target fails for natural quadratic energies, prove or at least sharply identify the obstruction.  An obstruction result is valuable if it explains which part of the PML coupling prevents monotonicity.
\end{enumerate}

The energy may include weighted \(L^2\) norms, cross terms, shifted variables, time-integrated auxiliary variables, polarization energy, fractional-memory energy, and derivative terms if they are mathematically justified.

\section{Model to Analyze}
\label{sec:model}

The model is the system shown in the supplied manuscript image.  Write
\[
  E=E_z,\qquad \epsilon_\infty=\epsilon_{r,\infty},\qquad
  \epsilon_s=\epsilon_{r,s},\qquad \mu=\mu_0\mu_r,
\]
and
\[
  \chi=\epsilon_0(\epsilon_s-\epsilon_\infty).
\]
The unknowns are
\[
  E,\quad H_x,\quad H_y,\quad P,\quad P_{z,1},\quad P_{z,2},\quad Q_x,\quad Q_y.
\]
The PML system is
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty\,\partial_t E
&= \partial_xH_y-\partial_yH_x
   -\epsilon_\infty(\sx+\sy)E
   -\partial_tP-\frac{\sx+\sy}{\epsilon_0}P
   +P_{z,1}+P_{z,2},\\
\mu\,\partial_tH_x
&= -\partial_yE-\mu\frac{\sy-\sx}{\epsilon_0}H_x+Q_x,\\
\mu\,\partial_tH_y
&= \partial_xE-\mu\frac{\sx-\sy}{\epsilon_0}H_y+Q_y,\\
P+\tau^\alpha\partial_t^\alpha P
&=\chi E,\\
\partial_tP_{z,1}
&=-\frac{\epsilon_\infty}{\epsilon_0}\sx\sy E,\\
\partial_tP_{z,2}
&=-\frac{\sx\sy}{\epsilon_0^2}P,\\
\partial_tQ_x
&=-\frac{\sx}{\epsilon_0}Q_x
  +\frac{\mu\sx(\sy-\sx)}{\epsilon_0^2}H_x,\\
\partial_tQ_y
&=-\frac{\sy}{\epsilon_0}Q_y
  +\frac{\mu\sy(\sx-\sy)}{\epsilon_0^2}H_y.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:main-model}
\end{equation}
Here \(\partial_t^\alpha\) should be interpreted as a Caputo-type fractional derivative when \(0<\alpha<1\).  The non-fractional case requested by the user is the case
\[
  \alpha=1,\qquad
  P+\tau\partial_tP=\chi E.
\]
Thus the first stage of the analysis should use \(\alpha=1\), not a model with \(P\) removed.

The boundary condition is the perfectly conducting boundary condition
\[
  \widehat n\times E=0\qquad\text{on }\partial\Om.
\]
For the two-dimensional TM model this should be interpreted as
\[
  E=E_z=0\qquad\text{on }\partial\Om,
\]
so that the Maxwell principal part has no positive boundary contribution.  If a proof uses a different boundary condition, it must state that choice explicitly.

\begin{remark}
The parameters \(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_\infty,\epsilon_s,\mu,\tau\) are positive, and \(\chi>0\) when \(\epsilon_s>\epsilon_\infty\).  The absorption parameters are time-independent and nonnegative.  The first serious cases to analyze are constant \(\sx,\sy\), then separated variable coefficients \(\sx(x),\sy(y)\), and only then general \(\sx(x,y),\sy(x,y)\).
\end{remark}

\section{First Energy Balance to Verify}

Start with the electromagnetic part
\[
  \Ecal_{\rm em}(t)=\frac12\int_\Om
  \left(\epsilon_0\epsilon_\infty E^2+\mu H_x^2+\mu H_y^2\right)\dd x\dd y.
\]

\begin{task}[Check the electromagnetic energy derivative]
Using \eqref{eq:main-model} and the PEC boundary condition, verify that the Maxwell principal part cancels by integration by parts, and that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\Ecal_{\rm em}
=\int_\Om\Big[
&-\epsilon_\infty(\sx+\sy)E^2
-E\partial_tP
-\frac{\sx+\sy}{\epsilon_0}EP
+E(P_{z,1}+P_{z,2})\\
&-\frac{\mu}{\epsilon_0}(\sy-\sx)H_x^2
-\frac{\mu}{\epsilon_0}(\sx-\sy)H_y^2
+H_xQ_x+H_yQ_y
\Big]\dd x\dd y .
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:em-balance}
\]
The terms involving \(H_x,H_y\) are sign-indefinite when \(\sx\ne\sy\).  The terms involving \(P,P_{z,1},P_{z,2}\) are the electric/PML auxiliary coupling terms that must be absorbed by a refined energy.
\end{task}

\section{The \texorpdfstring{\(\alpha=1\)}{alpha=1} Polarization Identity}

For the non-fractional case \(\alpha=1\),
\[
  P+\tau\partial_tP=\chi E,
\]
so
\[
  E=\frac{P+\tau\partial_tP}{\chi}.
\]
This gives the useful identity
\begin{equation}
  E\,\partial_tP
  =\frac{1}{2\chi}\frac{\dd}{\dd t}\|P\|_{L^2(\Om)}^2
   +\frac{\tau}{\chi}\|\partial_tP\|_{L^2(\Om)}^2.
\label{eq:alpha-one-dissipation}
\end{equation}

\begin{task}[Use the alpha=1 identity]
Use \eqref{eq:alpha-one-dissipation} to decide whether the energy
\[
  \Ecal_{\rm em+P}
  =\Ecal_{\rm em}+\frac{1}{2\chi}\|P\|_{L^2(\Om)}^2
\]
is the right starting point.  Then identify the remaining troublesome electric auxiliary terms:
\[
  -\frac{\sx+\sy}{\epsilon_0}EP,\qquad
  E P_{z,1},\qquad
  E P_{z,2},\qquad
  \partial_tP_{z,1},\qquad
  \partial_tP_{z,2}.
\]
Try to absorb them using cross terms, shifted variables, or time-integrated variables.
\end{task}

\section{Magnetic Auxiliary Variable Shift}

Define
\[
  a_x=\frac{\sy-\sx}{\epsilon_0},\qquad
  a_y=\frac{\sx-\sy}{\epsilon_0},\qquad
  b_x=\frac{\sx}{\epsilon_0},\qquad
  b_y=\frac{\sy}{\epsilon_0}.
\]
The magnetic equations and \(Q_x,Q_y\) equations suggest the shifted variables
\[
  M_x=Q_x-\mu a_xH_x,\qquad
  M_y=Q_y-\mu a_yH_y.
\]

\begin{task}[Verify shifted magnetic identities]
Starting from \eqref{eq:main-model}, verify
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\partial_tM_x
&= a_x\,\partial_yE-\frac{\sy}{\epsilon_0}M_x,\\
\partial_tM_y
&= -a_y\,\partial_xE-\frac{\sx}{\epsilon_0}M_y.
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:magnetic-shift}
\end{equation}
Then test whether an energy written in terms of \(H_x,H_y,M_x,M_y\), rather than \(H_x,H_y,Q_x,Q_y\), has a cleaner dissipation structure.
\end{task}

\begin{remark}
If \(\sx,\sy\) are spatially variable, \eqref{eq:magnetic-shift} itself does not produce \(\partial_t\sigma\) terms, because the coefficients are time-independent.  However, integrated energy identities may produce \(\partial_x\sx\), \(\partial_y\sy\), or general \(\nabla\sigma_i\) terms after integration by parts.  These terms are likely to be one source of bounded-but-not-monotone estimates.
\end{remark}

\section{Electric PML Auxiliary Variables}

The variables \(P_{z,1}\) and \(P_{z,2}\) satisfy
\[
  \partial_tP_{z,1}=-\frac{\epsilon_\infty}{\epsilon_0}\sx\sy E,\qquad
  \partial_tP_{z,2}=-\frac{\sx\sy}{\epsilon_0^2}P.
\]
They appear in the \(E\)-equation as \(E(P_{z,1}+P_{z,2})\).  This resembles the need for time-integrated or cross-term energies in PML analyses.

\begin{task}[Handle Pz1 and Pz2]
Try the following routes:
\begin{enumerate}
\item define time-integrated variables
\[
  R_1(t)=\int_0^tP_{z,1}(s)\dd s,\qquad
  R_2(t)=\int_0^tP_{z,2}(s)\dd s;
\]
\item add cross terms such as \((E,P_{z,1})\), \((P,P_{z,2})\), or weighted combinations;
\item freeze \(\sx,\sy\) as constants and solve the pointwise Lyapunov matrix problem for the electric subsystem \((E,P,P_{z,1},P_{z,2})\);
\item identify whether the corner factor \(\sx\sy\) is the essential obstruction.
\end{enumerate}
\end{task}

\section{Baffet-Type Energy Design Clue}

Baffet--Grote--Imperiale--Kachanovska proved monotone energy decay for a second-order wave-equation PML with constant damping coefficients\cite{baffetGroteImperialeKachanovska2019}.  Their main lesson is methodological: do not start from the naive energy alone.  In two dimensions they introduce
\[
  \lambda=\nabla u+\phi,\qquad
  a=\operatorname{tr}\Gamma_1,\qquad
  b=\det\Gamma_1,
\]
and use an energy of the form
\[
  E[u,\phi]=\frac12\left(
  \|\partial_tu+a u\|^2+\|\nabla u+\phi\|^2
  +\|\phi\|^2_{a^{-1}\Gamma_1}+\|u\|^2_b\right).
\]
In three dimensions they further introduce time-integrated auxiliary variables \(\Phi,\Psi\) and a shifted variable \(q\).

\begin{task}[Translate the Baffet idea to \eqref{eq:main-model}]
Look for Maxwell--PML analogues of the following structures:
\begin{itemize}
\item shifted field variables analogous to \(\partial_tu+a u\);
\item combinations of principal variables and PML auxiliaries analogous to \(\nabla u+\phi\);
\item time-integrated variables such as \(\int_0^tP_{z,1}\dd s\), \(\int_0^tP_{z,2}\dd s\), \(\int_0^tQ_x\dd s\), \(\int_0^tQ_y\dd s\);
\item cross terms that turn \(E P_{z,1}\), \(E P_{z,2}\), \(H_xQ_x\), \(H_yQ_y\) into exact time derivatives plus nonpositive remainders.
\end{itemize}
Any candidate energy must be checked for positive definiteness and boundary contributions.
\end{task}

## statement

If a physical subregion has zero PML damping, then E=0, P=0, all PML auxiliary variables zero, and H=(H_x,H_y)=grad phi with phi smooth and compactly supported in that undamped physical subregion gives an exact stationary Maxwell-Debye solution whenever curl H=partial_x H_y-partial_y H_x=0. The magnetic energy is positive for grad phi nonzero while all layer and Debye damping terms vanish. Hence no positive total energy controlling the magnetic field can be strictly decreasing for every nonzero state on the whole computational domain; any dissipative identity must have a characterized nullspace containing such undamped stationary modes. See artifacts/proofs/stage3_repaired_model_energy.md.

The formulation uses a time primitive of the electric field\nand a time primitive of the Debye polarization, which is exactly the type of\naugmented/time-integrated variable used in Baffet-type PML energy arguments.\n\n## Assumptions and notation\n\nLet\n\\[\ne=\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty>0,\\quad \\mu>0,\\quad \\chi>0,\\quad \\tau>0.\n\\]\nIn the Laplace domain,\n\\[\n\\varepsilon_D(s)=e+\\frac{\\chi}{1+\\tau s}.\n\\]\nOn one constant-coefficient PML block let\n\\[\n\\sigma_x,\\sigma_y\\ge 0,\\qquad\na=\\sigma_x+\\sigma_y,\\qquad b=\\sigma_x\\sigma_y,\n\\]\nand assume \\(a>0\\) for the PML block.  The undamped physical block \\(a=b=0\\)\nuses the ordinary Maxwell-Debye energy and is coupled by the usual transmission\nflux.  Define\n\\[\n\\Gamma_1=\\begin{pmatrix}\\sigma_x&0\\\\0&\\sigma_y\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad\n\\Gamma_2=\\begin{pmatrix}\\sigma_y-\\sigma_x&0\\\\0&\\sigma_x-\\sigma_y\\end{pmatrix}.\n\\]\nFor a vector \\(v\\), write \\(|v|_M^2=v\\cdot Mv\\).\n\nLet \\(u\\) be the time primitive of the electric field:\n\\[\nE=u_t.\n\\]\nLet \\(q\\) be the time primitive of the Debye polarization:\n\\[\nq_t=P.\n\\]\nThe Debye law is written in compatible primitive form\n\\[\n\\tau P_t+P=\\chi u_t,\\qquad q+\\tau P=\\chi u.\n\\]\nThe second relation is preserved by the first two equations if it is true at\ninitial time.\n\n## Baffet-type matched PML system\n\nIntroduce the Baffet auxiliary vector \\(\\phi=(\\phi_x,\\phi_y)\\) and\n\\[\n\\lambda=\\nabla u+\\phi.\n\\]\nThe constant-coefficient two-dimensional repaired model is\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mu\\{e(u_{tt}+a u_t+b u)+P_t+aP+bq\\}-\\nabla\\cdot\\lambda=0,}\n\\tag{1}\n\\]\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\phi_t+\\Gamma_1\\phi=\\Gamma_2\\nabla u,}\n\\tag{2}\n\\]\n\\[\n\\boxed{\\tau P_t+P=\\chi u_t,\\qquad q_t=P,\\qquad q+\\tau P=\\chi u.}\n\\tag{3}\n\\]\nOuter boundary conditions are taken so that the boundary flux\n\\[\n\\int_{\\partial\\Omega}(u_t+au)\\lambda\\cdot n\\,ds\n\\]\nis zero or nonpositive.  For a PEC outer boundary, the compatible primitive\ncondition is \\(u=0\\), hence \\(u_t=E=0\\), on that boundary.  On piecewise\nconstant internal interfaces, the usual transmission conditions are continuity\nof \\(u\\) and \\(\\lambda\\cdot n\\), so the flux cancels pairwise.\n\n## Equivalence with the stretched-coordinate Maxwell-Debye PML\n\nFor constant coefficients, Laplace transforming (2) gives\n\\[\n\\widehat\\phi_x=\\frac{\\sigma_y-\\sigma_x}{s+\\sigma_x}\\partial_x\\widehat u,\n\\qquad\n\\widehat\\phi_y=\\frac{\\sigma_x-\\sigma_y}{s+\\sigma_y}\\partial_y\\widehat u.\n\\]\nThus\n\\[\n\\widehat\\lambda_x\n=\\frac{s+\\sigma_y}{s+\\sigma_x}\\partial_x\\widehat u\n=\\frac{S_y}{S_x}\\partial_x\\widehat u,\\qquad\n\\widehat\\lambda_y\n=\\frac{s+\\sigma_x}{s+\\sigma_y}\\partial_y\\widehat u\n=\\frac{S_x}{S_y}\\partial_y\\widehat u,\n\\]\nwhere\n\\[\nS_i(s)=1+\\frac{\\sigma_i}{s}=\\frac{s+\\sigma_i}{s}.\n\\]\nThe Debye compatibility gives\n\\[\n\\widehat P=\\frac{\\chi s}{1+\\tau s}\\widehat u,\\qquad\n\\widehat q=\\frac{1}{s}\\widehat P.\n\\]\nTherefore\n\\[\ne(s^2+as+b)\\widehat u+s\\widehat P+a\\widehat P+b\\widehat q\n=\\left(e+\\frac{\\chi}{1+\\tau s}\\right)(s^2+as+b)\\widehat u\n=\\varepsilon_D(s)s^2S_xS_y\\widehat u.\n\\]\nEquation (1) becomes\n\\[\n\\mu\\varepsilon_D(s)s^2S_xS_y\\widehat u\n=\\nabla\\cdot\\widehat\\lambda.\n\\]\nDividing by \\(S_xS_y\\) gives\n\\[\n\\mu\\varepsilon_D(s)s^2\\widehat u\n=S_x^{-1}\\partial_x(S_x^{-1}\\partial_x\\widehat u)\n+S_y^{-1}\\partial_y(S_y^{-1}\\partial_y\\widehat u).\n\\]\nSince \\(\\widehat E=s\\widehat u\\), this is exactly the second-order equation\nobtained by eliminating \\(H_x,H_y\\) from the standard stretched-coordinate\nMaxwell-Debye PML while keeping\n\\[\n(1+\\tau s)\\widehat P=\\chi \\widehat E.\n\\]\nConsequently this Baffet-type time-domain system has the same planar-interface\nperfect matching as the standard stretched-coordinate PML: at an \\(x\\)-interface\nwith \\(S_y=1\\), the normal symbol satisfies \\(\\nu=S_x\\nu_0\\) and the tangential\nMaxwell admittance is unchanged.\n\n## Energy functional\n\nDefine\n\\[\n\\alpha=1+2a\\tau,\\qquad\n\\beta=a+b\\tau,\\qquad\n\\gamma=a^2+b(1+a\\tau).\n\\]\nThe Baffet-Debye energy is\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\mathcal E_{BD}\n=\\frac12\\int_\\Omega \\{&\n\\mu e(u_t+a u)^2+|\\lambda|^2\n+|\\phi|_{a^{-1}\\Gamma_1}^2+\\mu e\\,b u^2\\\\\n&+\\frac{\\mu}{\\chi}\\left(\\alpha P^2+2\\beta Pq+\\gamma q^2\\right)\n\\}\\,dxdy .\n\\end{aligned}}\n\\tag{4}\n\\]\nThe \\(P,q\\) block is positive definite whenever \\(a>0\\).  Indeed\n\\[\n\\alpha>0,\\qquad\n\\alpha\\gamma-\\beta^2\n=b+ab\\tau+2a^3\\tau+b(2a^2-b)\\tau^2>0,\n\\]\nbecause \\(a=\\sigma_x+\\sigma_y>0\\), \\(b=\\sigma_x\\sigma_y\\ge0\\), \\(\\tau>0\\), and\n\\(2a^2-b\\ge0\\).  Thus (4) is nonnegative, and it is coercive on the PML block\nmodulo the usual zero modes of the primitive variables and boundary conditions.\n\n## Energy identity\n\nTest (1) with \\(u_t+a u\\).  The nondispersive part gives the usual Baffet\ncalculation:\n\\[\n\\frac12\\frac{d}{dt}\\int_\\Omega\n\\mu e\\{(u_t+a u)^2+b u^2\\}\\,dxdy\n+\\int_\\Omega \\mu e\\,ab u^2\\,dxdy\n=\\int_\\Omega (u_t+a u)\\nabla\\cdot\\lambda\\,dxdy\n-\\mu\\int_\\Omega (P_t+aP+bq)(u_t+a u)\\,dxdy .\n\\tag{5}\n\\]\nThe boundary part of the first term is the flux stated above, and the interior\npart is handled by the same Baffet multiplier used for \\(\\lambda\\).  Specifically,\nfrom\n\\[\n\\lambda_t+\\Gamma_1\\lambda=\\nabla u_t+\\widetilde\\Gamma_2\\nabla u,\\qquad\n\\widetilde\\Gamma_2=\\Gamma_2+\\Gamma_1\n=\\begin{pmatrix}\\sigma_y&0\\\\0&\\sigma_x\\end{pmatrix},\n\\]\nand the multiplier\n\\[\ng=(I+a^{-1}\\Gamma_1)\\lambda-a^{-1}\\Gamma_1\\nabla u,\n\\]\none obtains\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n&\\frac12\\frac{d}{dt}\\int_\\Omega\n\\left(|\\lambda|^2+|\\phi|_{a^{-1}\\Gamma_1}^2\\right)\\,dxdy\\\\\n&\\quad+\\int_\\Omega\n\\left(|\\lambda|^2_{\\Gamma_1(I+a^{-1}\\Gamma_1)}\n+\\frac{b}{a}|\\nabla u|^2\\right)\\,dxdy\n=\\int_\\Omega \\nabla(u_t+a u)\\cdot\\lambda\\,dxdy .\n\\end{aligned}\n\\tag{6}\n\\]\nThis is the two-dimensional Baffet identity; it uses\n\\(\\Gamma_1\\widetilde\\Gamma_2=bI\\) and\n\\(a^{-1}\\Gamma_1(\\Gamma_1+\\widetilde\\Gamma_2)+\\widetilde\\Gamma_2=aI\\).\n\nIt remains to compute the Debye primitive contribution.  Using\n\\[\nu_t+a u\n=\\frac{\\tau P_t+(1+a\\tau)P+a q}{\\chi},\n\\]\nwe have\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n&(P_t+aP+bq)(u_t+a u)\\\\\n&=\\frac1\\chi\\Big[\n\\frac12\\frac{d}{dt}\n\\left(\\alpha P^2+2\\beta Pq+\\gamma q^2\\right)\n+\\tau P_t^2+\\tau(a^2-b)P^2+abq^2\n\\Big].\n\\end{aligned}\n\\tag{7}\n\\]\nHere \\(q_t=P\\), and the constants \\(\\alpha,\\beta,\\gamma\\) are exactly those in\n(4).\n\nAdding (5), (6), and (7) gives the full identity\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{d}{dt}\\mathcal E_{BD}(t)\n=-\\mathcal D_{BD}(t)\n+\\int_{\\partial\\Omega}(u_t+a u)\\lambda\\cdot n\\,ds,}\n\\tag{8}\n\\]\nwhere\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\mathcal D_{BD}\n=\\int_\\Omega \\{&\n|\\lambda|^2_{\\Gamma_1(I+a^{-1}\\Gamma_1)}\n+\\frac{b}{a}|\\nabla u|^2+\\mu e\\,ab u^2\\\\\n&+\\frac{\\mu}{\\chi}\\left[\n\\tau P_t^2+\\tau(a^2-b)P^2+abq^2\n\\right]\\}\\,dxdy .\n\\end{aligned}}\n\\tag{9}\n\\]\nAll displayed terms in \\(\\mathcal D_{BD}\\) are nonnegative for\n\\(\\sigma_x,\\sigma_y\\ge0\\), \\(a>0\\), and positive material parameters.  Under PEC\nor canceling transmission flux, (8) gives\n\\[\n\\mathcal E_{BD}(t)+\\int_0^t\\mathcal D_{BD}(r)\\,dr\\le \\mathcal E_{BD}(0).\n\\]\n\n## Classification and nullspace\n\nThis is a full two-dimensional constant-coefficient dissipative identity for an\nexact stretched-coordinate Maxwell-Debye PML, written in Baffet-type\ntime-integrated variables.  It is non-increasing, not strictly decreasing on the\nwhole computational domain.  The nullspace contains the already identified\nundamped physical-region stationary magnetic modes; in the PML block, the\ndissipation also leaves the standard primitive-variable gauge modes unless fixed\nby boundary/transmission compatibility.  Thus the sharp statement is\nnon-increase plus a characterized nullspace/no-abnormal-growth estimate, not\nstrict decay of every nonzero whole-domain state.\n\nFor spatially varying damping profiles, this artifact does not claim an energy\nidentity.  As in the Baffet reference, the verified scope is constant\ncoefficients, and piecewise constant layers are handled blockwise with\ntransmission flux cancellation.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
./verification/agent_runs/verify-20260620T072508563237Z-fact-a-baffet-type-time-primitive-standa/codex.events.jsonl:17:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_6","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/zsh -lc \"sed -n '1,320p' artifacts/proofs/stage3_repaired_model_energy.md\"","aggregated_output":"# Stage-3 proof: repaired PML candidates and dissipative-energy classification\n\nProblem id: `2d_maxwell_pml_energy_functional_exploration`\n\nTask: `task-stage3-repaired-model-energy`\n\n## Input fact from the matching test\n\nThe v2 covariantly damped Maxwell--Debye model has the verified stage-2 monotone\nenergy identity, but the stage-3 interface calculation shows that it is not a\nperfectly matched layer.  In an \\(x\\)-layer with \\(\\rho_x=\\rho>0,\\rho_y=0\\),\n\\[\nY_{v2}^2-Y_0^2\n=-\\frac{\\rho}{\\mu^2}\\left[\n\\frac{\\mu\\chi\\tau}{(1+\\tau s)(1+\\tau(s+\\rho))}\n+\\frac{k_y^2}{s^2(s+\\rho)}\n\\right],\n\\]\nso the v2 reflection coefficient is not identically zero.\n\nTherefore a repaired model must keep the physical Debye law as a function of the\nLaplace variable \\(s\\), not \\(s+\\rho\\), and must implement damping through\ncoordinate stretching or an equivalent split/ADE system.\n\n## Candidate 1: classical stretched-coordinate Maxwell--Debye PML\n\nLet\n\\[\n\\varepsilon_D(s)=\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty+\\frac{\\chi}{1+\\tau s},\n\\qquad\nS_i(s)=1+\\frac{\\sigma_i}{s},\\quad i=x,y.\n\\]\nIn the physical region \\(\\sigma_x=\\sigma_y=0\\).  In the PML the coefficients are\nnonnegative and are first analyzed as piecewise constant near each planar\ninterface.\n\nThe Laplace-domain repaired model is\n\\[\n\\boxed{\ns\\varepsilon_D(s)\\widehat E\n=S_x^{-1}\\partial_x\\widehat H_y\n-S_y^{-1}\\partial_y\\widehat H_x,}\n\\]\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mu s\\widehat H_x=-S_y^{-1}\\partial_y\\widehat E,\\qquad\n\\mu s\\widehat H_y=S_x^{-1}\\partial_x\\widehat E,}\n\\]\n\\[\n\\boxed{(1+\\tau s)\\widehat P=\\chi\\widehat E.}\n\\]\nEquivalently, the Debye law is not damped:\n\\[\nP+\\tau P_t=\\chi E.\n\\]\n\n### Perfect matching\n\nAt an \\(x\\)-interface, \\(S_y=1\\).  With tangential Fourier number \\(k_y\\),\nthe physical normal symbol satisfies\n\\[\n\\nu_0^2=k_y^2+\\mu s^2\\varepsilon_D(s),\\qquad\nY_0=\\frac{\\nu_0}{\\mu s}.\n\\]\nIn the PML,\n\\[\ns\\varepsilon_D E=S_x^{-1}\\nu H_y-ik_yH_x,\\qquad\n\\mu sH_x=-ik_yE,\\qquad\n\\mu sH_y=S_x^{-1}\\nu E.\n\\]\nThe dispersion relation gives\n\\[\n\\left(S_x^{-1}\\nu\\right)^2=k_y^2+\\mu s^2\\varepsilon_D(s),\n\\]\nhence \\(\\nu=S_x\\nu_0\\) and\n\\[\nY_+=\\frac{S_x^{-1}\\nu}{\\mu s}=\\frac{\\nu_0}{\\mu s}=Y_0.\n\\]\nThus the planar-interface reflection coefficient is \\(R=0\\) for every\n\\((s,k_y)\\) in the Laplace half-plane.  The same argument applies to a\n\\(y\\)-interface with \\(x,y\\) interchanged.\n\n### Time-domain ADE realization\n\nDefine the causal operator\n\\[\n\\mathcal A_i=S_i^{-1}=\\frac{s}{s+\\sigma_i}\n\\]\nin the Laplace domain.  Equivalently,\n\\[\n\\mathcal A_i f=f+\\psi_i,\\qquad\n(\\partial_t+\\sigma_i)\\psi_i=-\\sigma_i f.\n\\]\nThen a time-domain unsplit ADE form is\n\\[\n\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty E_t+P_t\n=\\partial_xH_y-\\partial_yH_x\n+\\psi_{E,x}-\\psi_{E,y},\n\\]\n\\[\n\\mu H_{x,t}=-\\partial_yE-\\psi_{H_x,y},\\qquad\n\\mu H_{y,t}=\\partial_xE+\\psi_{H_y,x},\n\\]\n\\[\nP+\\tau P_t=\\chi E,\n\\]\nwith\n\\[\n(\\partial_t+\\sigma_x)\\psi_{E,x}=-\\sigma_x\\partial_xH_y,\\qquad\n(\\partial_t+\\sigma_y)\\psi_{E,y}=-\\sigma_y\\partial_yH_x,\n\\]\n\\[\n(\\partial_t+\\sigma_y)\\psi_{H_x,y}=-\\sigma_y\\partial_yE,\\qquad\n(\\partial_t+\\sigma_x)\\psi_{H_y,x}=-\\sigma_x\\partial_xE.\n\\]\nInterface conditions are continuity of the physical tangential traces.  For an\n\\(x\\)-interface these are \\(E\\) and \\(H_y\\).  The auxiliary variables vanish in the\nphysical region and are initialized consistently with the causal convolution.\n\n### Naive energy calculation\n\nThe natural physical Debye energy is\n\\[\n\\mathcal E_{\\rm phys}\n=\\frac12\\int_\\Omega\n\\left(\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty E^2+\\mu H_x^2+\\mu H_y^2+\\chi^{-1}P^2\\right)\\,dxdy.\n\\]\nIt is positive because\n\\(\\epsilon_0,\\epsilon_\\infty,\\mu,\\chi>0\\).  Using\n\\[\nE P_t=\\frac{1}{2\\chi}\\partial_t(P^2)+\\frac{\\tau}{\\chi}P_t^2\n\\]\nand the PEC boundary condition \\(E=0\\) on the outer boundary gives\n\\[\n\\frac{d}{dt}\\mathcal E_{\\rm phys}\n=-\\int_\\Omega\\frac{\\tau}{\\chi}P_t^2\\,dxdy\n+\\int_\\Omega\n\\left[\nE(\\psi_{E,x}-\\psi_{E,y})\n-H_x\\psi_{H_x,y}\n+H_y\\psi_{H_y,x}\n\\right]\\,dxdy .\n\\]\nThe Maxwell principal part contributes only the boundary flux\n\\[\n\\int_{\\partial\\Omega}E(H_y n_x-H_x n_y)\\,ds,\n\\]\nwhich vanishes under PEC at the outer boundary and cancels by transmission at\ninternal material/PML interfaces when the tangential traces are continuous.\n\nThe remaining auxiliary terms are not sign-definite in this naive energy.\nTherefore the positive physical Debye energy alone is not a monotone energy for\nthe exact stretched-coordinate PML.\n\n### Classification\n\nThis candidate is the formula-level perfect-matching repair.  A local monotone\nenergy for the full 2D Maxwell--Debye ADE system is not certified here.  The\ncalculation above identifies the exact terms that a Baffet-type augmented energy\nwould have to absorb:\n\\[\nE\\psi_{E,x},\\quad E\\psi_{E,y},\\quad\nH_x\\psi_{H_x,y},\\quad H_y\\psi_{H_y,x}.\n\\]\nThe literature record supports that such augmented energies are non-naive and\nthat constant-coefficient damping is the natural first scope for a sharp identity.\n\n### Reduced normal-incidence 1D energy identity\n\nThere is one important positive result for the exact stretched-coordinate model.\nIn the \\(x\\)-layer normal-incidence block \\(k_y=0\\), the standard stretch gives\n\\[\n(\\partial_t+\\rho)(\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty E+P)=\\partial_xH_y,\n\\qquad\n\\mu(\\partial_t+\\rho)H_y=\\partial_xE,\n\\]\n\\[\nP+\\tau P_t=\\chi E.\n\\]\nThis is exactly the \\(k_y=0\\) restriction of the perfectly matched stretched\nmodel, not the v2 model, because the Debye law still uses \\(\\partial_t\\) rather\nthan \\(\\partial_t+\\rho\\).\n\nMultiply the first equation by \\(E\\), the second by \\(H_y\\), and use\n\\[\nE=\\frac{P+\\tau P_t}{\\chi}.\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\nE P_t=\\frac{1}{2\\chi}\\partial_t(P^2)+\\frac{\\tau}{\\chi}P_t^2,\n\\]\nand\n\\[\n\\rho E P\n=\\frac{\\rho}{\\chi}P^2+\\frac{\\rho\\tau}{2\\chi}\\partial_t(P^2).\n\\]\nAfter integrating by parts, the principal terms give only the boundary flux\n\\(\\int_{\\partial I}EH_y n_x\\,ds\\).  Hence\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\frac{d}{dt}\\mathcal E_{1d,sc}\n=-\\int_I\\left(\n\\rho\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty E^2+\\mu\\rho H_y^2\n+\\frac{\\rho}{\\chi}P^2+\\frac{\\tau}{\\chi}P_t^2\n\\right)\\,dx\n+\\int_{\\partial I}EH_y n_x\\,ds,}\n\\]\nwhere\n\\[\n\\boxed{\n\\mathcal E_{1d,sc}\n=\\frac12\\int_I\\left(\n\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty E^2+\\mu H_y^2\n+\\frac{1+\\rho\\tau}{\\chi}P^2\n\\right)\\,dx.}\n\\]\nThis energy is positive for \\(\\rho,\\tau,\\chi>0\\), and it is dissipative under\nPEC or otherwise nonpositive boundary flux.  It explains why the v2 idea is\nclose to a useful construction in normal incidence, but it does not solve the\nfull 2D oblique problem: as soon as \\(k_y\\ne0\\), the exact stretched model\ncontains the ADE memory couplings displayed above.\n\n## Candidate 2: generalized CFS/ADE stretched-coordinate PML\n\nLet\n\\[\nS_i(s)=\\kappa_i+\\frac{\\sigma_i}{s+\\alpha_i},\n\\qquad\n\\kappa_i\\ge1,\\quad \\sigma_i\\ge0,\\quad \\alpha_i\\ge0.\n\\]\nThe repaired Laplace-domain equations are the same as Candidate 1, with these\n\\(S_i\\).  In particular the Debye law remains\n\\[\n(1+\\tau s)\\widehat P=\\chi\\widehat E.\n\\]\n\nFor a planar \\(x\\)-interface with \\(S_y=1\\), the same calculation gives\n\\[\n\\nu=S_x\\nu_0,\\qquad Y_+=Y_0,\n\\]\nso the continuous model is perfectly matched whenever the stretch is applied to\nthe spatial derivatives and the physical material law is left unchanged.\n\nIf \\(S_i^{-1}\\) is rational with poles in \\(\\Re s<0\\), it can be implemented by\nADE variables.  The CFS shift \\(\\alpha_i>0\\) is a standard way to improve\nlow-frequency/evanescent and late-time behavior, but a monotone time-domain\nenergy requires an explicit positive realization of the memory kernel.  No such\npositive memory theorem is claimed here for the full 2D Maxwell--Debye system.\n\nClassification: perfectly matched at the continuous planar-interface level;\nrecommended if long-time CFS behavior is needed; energy status is boundedness or\npassive-memory proof pending, not a completed monotone identity.\n\n## Candidate 3: MPML-type extra damping\n\nAn MPML-type repair adds damping in more than the normal coordinate direction.\nFor example, in an \\(x\\)-layer one may replace a scalar stretch by a multiaxial\nstretch depending also on tangential damping parameters.  This is useful for\nremoving long-time instabilities or Jordan-block behavior in some systems.\n\nHowever, if the tangential stretch is nontrivial at the physical/PML interface,\nthe planar admittance generally changes.  The MPML literature inspected for this\nrun explicitly treats MPML as a stability-oriented absorbing layer and records\nthat exact perfect matching may be lost in multiaxial variants.\n\nClassification: absorbing/stability repair, not the primary exact-matching\nrepair for the present Maxwell--Debye interface theorem.\n\n## Complete dissipative identity that is currently verified\n\nThe only complete positive monotone identity verified in the existing Iteris\nmemory is for the v2 covariantly damped absorbing layer:\n\\[\n\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty D_\\rho E\n=\\partial_xH_y-\\partial_yH_x-D_\\rho P,\n\\]\n\\[\n\\mu(\\partial_t+\\rho_y)H_x=-\\partial_yE,\\qquad\n\\mu(\\partial_t+\\rho_x)H_y=\\partial_xE,\n\\]\n\\[\nP+\\tau D_\\rho P=\\chi E,\\qquad D_\\rho=\\partial_t+\\rho_x+\\rho_y.\n\\]\nIts energy is\n\\[\n\\mathcal E_\\rho(t)=\\frac12\\int_\\Omega\n\\left(\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty E^2+\\mu H_x^2+\\mu H_y^2+\\chi^{-1}P^2\\right)\\,dxdy\n\\]\nand the verified identity is\n\\[\n\\frac{d}{dt}\\mathcal E_\\rho(t)\n=-\\int_\\Omega\\left(\n\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty\\rho E^2\n+\\mu\\rho_yH_x^2\n+\\mu\\rho_xH_y^2\n+\\frac{\\rho}{\\chi}P^2\n+\\frac{\\tau}{\\chi}|D_\\rho P|^2\n\\right)\\,dxdy.\n\\]\nThis identity is genuinely dissipative, but the model is not perfectly matched.\nIt should therefore be described as a stable absorbing-layer model, not as a\nstandard PML.\n\n## Formula-level obstruction to strict decay on the whole domain\n\nEven for a perfectly matched repair, strict decay of a total energy controlling\nall fields on the whole computational domain cannot hold without a nullspace.\nAssume a physical subregion where \\(\\sigma_x=\\sigma_y=0\\) and choose\n\\[\nE=0,\\qquad P=0,\\qquad H_x=\\partial_x\\phi,\\qquad H_y=\\partial_y\\phi,\n\\]\nwith \\(\\phi\\) smooth and compactly supported inside that undamped physical\nsubregion. The system to be analyzed is the two-dimensional TM Maxwell--PML model with polarization \\(P\\), PML auxiliary variables \\(P_{z,1},P_{z,2},Q_x,Q_y\\), and perfectly conducting boundary condition.  The first target is to find a genuinely monotone decreasing energy functional in two space dimensions.  If such a monotone energy cannot be found, the fallback target is to find a positive energy functional that proves boundedness/no abnormal long-time growth, in the same spirit as the long-time-stability role of MPML.  The non-fractional case should be understood as the special case \\(\\alpha=1\\) of the displayed polarization law.\n\\end{abstract}\n\n\\section{Primary Goal}\n\nLet \\(\\Om\\subset\\R^2\\) be a rectangular computational domain containing a physical region and a PML layer.  The absorption parameters are\n\\[\n  \\sx=\\sx(x)\\ge0,\\qquad \\sy=\\sy(y)\\ge0,\n\\]\nor, in a harder variant,\n\\[\n  \\sx=\\sx(x,y)\\ge0,\\qquad \\sy=\\sy(x,y)\\ge0.\n\\]\nThe main goal is to analyze the two-dimensional system in Section~\\ref{sec:model} and construct an energy functional \\(\\Ecal(t)\\).\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n\\item \\textbf{Strong target: monotone decreasing energy.}\nFind a positive energy functional such that\n\\[\n  \\frac{\\dd}{\\dd t}\\Ecal(t)=-\\Dcal(t)\\le0.\n\\]\nThis is the preferred outcome.\n\\item \\textbf{Fallback target: bounded/non-growing energy.}\nIf no monotone energy can be found, find a positive energy functional that rules out abnormal growth from the PML layer, for example\n\\[\n  \\Ecal(t)\\le C\\,\\Ecal(0)\n\\]\nwith \\(C\\) independent of long time if possible. An obstruction result is valuable if it explains which part of the PML coupling prevents monotonicity.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nThe energy may include weighted \\(L^2\\) norms, cross terms, shifted variables, time-integrated auxiliary variables, polarization energy, fractional-memory energy, and derivative terms if they are mathematically justified.\n\n\\section{Model to Analyze}\n\\label{sec:model}\n\nThe model is the system shown in the supplied manuscript image.  Write\n\\[\n  E=E_z,\\qquad \\epsilon_\\infty=\\epsilon_{r,\\infty},\\qquad\n  \\epsilon_s=\\epsilon_{r,s},\\qquad \\mu=\\mu_0\\mu_r,\n\\]\nand\n\\[\n  \\chi=\\epsilon_0(\\epsilon_s-\\epsilon_\\infty).\n\\]\nThe unknowns are\n\\[\n  E,\\quad H_x,\\quad H_y,\\quad P,\\quad P_{z,1},\\quad P_{z,2},\\quad Q_x,\\quad Q_y.\n\\]\nThe PML system is\n\\begin{equation}\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty\\,\\partial_t E\n&= \\partial_xH_y-\\partial_yH_x\n   -\\epsilon_\\infty(\\sx+\\sy)E\n   -\\partial_tP-\\frac{\\sx+\\sy}{\\epsilon_0}P\n   +P_{z,1}+P_{z,2},\\\\\n\\mu\\,\\partial_tH_x\n&= -\\partial_yE-\\mu\\frac{\\sy-\\sx}{\\epsilon_0}H_x+Q_x,\\\\\n\\mu\\,\\partial_tH_y\n&= \\partial_xE-\\mu\\frac{\\sx-\\sy}{\\epsilon_0}H_y+Q_y,\\\\\nP+\\tau^\\alpha\\partial_t^\\alpha P\n&=\\chi E,\\\\\n\\partial_tP_{z,1}\n&=-\\frac{\\epsilon_\\infty}{\\epsilon_0}\\sx\\sy E,\\\\\n\\partial_tP_{z,2}\n&=-\\frac{\\sx\\sy}{\\epsilon_0^2}P,\\\\\n\\partial_tQ_x\n&=-\\frac{\\sx}{\\epsilon_0}Q_x\n  +\\frac{\\mu\\sx(\\sy-\\sx)}{\\epsilon_0^2}H_x,\\\\\n\\partial_tQ_y\n&=-\\frac{\\sy}{\\epsilon_0}Q_y\n  +\\frac{\\mu\\sy(\\sx-\\sy)}{\\epsilon_0^2}H_y.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\label{eq:main-model}\n\\end{equation}\nHere \\(\\partial_t^\\alpha\\) should be interpreted as a Caputo-type fractional derivative when \\(0<\\alpha<1\\).  The non-fractional case requested by the user is the case\n\\[\n  \\alpha=1,\\qquad\n  P+\\tau\\partial_tP=\\chi E.\n\\]\nThus the first stage of the analysis should use \\(\\alpha=1\\), not a model with \\(P\\) removed.\n\nThe boundary condition is the perfectly conducting boundary condition\n\\[\n  \\widehat n\\times E=0\\qquad\\text{on }\\partial\\Om.\n\\]\nFor the two-dimensional TM model this should be interpreted as\n\\[\n  E=E_z=0\\qquad\\text{on }\\partial\\Om,\n\\]\nso that the Maxwell principal part has no positive boundary contribution.  If a proof uses a different boundary condition, it must state that choice explicitly.\n\n\\begin{remark}\nThe parameters \\(\\epsilon_0,\\epsilon_\\infty,\\epsilon_s,\\mu,\\tau\\) are positive, and \\(\\chi>0\\) when \\(\\epsilon_s>\\epsilon_\\infty\\).  The absorption parameters are time-independent and nonnegative.  The first serious cases to analyze are constant \\(\\sx,\\sy\\), then separated variable coefficients \\(\\sx(x),\\sy(y)\\), and only then general \\(\\sx(x,y),\\sy(x,y)\\).\n\\end{remark}\n\n\\section{First Energy Balance to Verify}\n\nStart with the electromagnetic part\n\\[\n  \\Ecal_{\\rm em}(t)=\\frac12\\int_\\Om\n  \\left(\\epsilon_0\\epsilon_\\infty E^2+\\mu H_x^2+\\mu H_y^2\\right)\\dd x\\dd y.\n\\]\n\n\\begin{task}[Check the electromagnetic energy derivative]\nUsing \\eqref{eq:main-model} and the PEC boundary condition, verify that the Maxwell principal part cancels by integration by parts, and that\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\frac{\\dd}{\\dd t}\\Ecal_{\\rm em}\n=\\int_\\Om\\Big[\n&-\\epsilon_\\infty(\\sx+\\sy)E^2\n-E\\partial_tP\n-\\frac{\\sx+\\sy}{\\epsilon_0}EP\n+E(P_{z,1}+P_{z,2})\\\\\n&-\\frac{\\mu}{\\epsilon_0}(\\sy-\\sx)H_x^2\n-\\frac{\\mu}{\\epsilon_0}(\\sx-\\sy)H_y^2\n+H_xQ_x+H_yQ_y\n\\Big]\\dd x\\dd y .\n\\end{aligned}\n\\label{eq:em-balance}\n\\]\nThe terms involving \\(H_x,H_y\\) are sign-indefinite when \\(\\sx\\ne\\sy\\). Then identify the remaining troublesome electric auxiliary terms:\n\\[\n  -\\frac{\\sx+\\sy}{\\epsilon_0}EP,\\qquad\n  E P_{z,1},\\qquad\n  E P_{z,2},\\qquad\n  \\partial_tP_{z,1},\\qquad\n  \\partial_tP_{z,2}.\n\\]\nTry to absorb them using cross terms, shifted variables, or time-integrated variables.\n\\end{task}\n\n\\section{Magnetic Auxiliary Variable Shift}\n\nDefine\n\\[\n  a_x=\\frac{\\sy-\\sx}{\\epsilon_0},\\qquad\n  a_y=\\frac{\\sx-\\sy}{\\epsilon_0},\\qquad\n  b_x=\\frac{\\sx}{\\epsilon_0},\\qquad\n  b_y=\\frac{\\sy}{\\epsilon_0}.\n\\]\nThe magnetic equations and \\(Q_x,Q_y\\) equations suggest the shifted variables\n\\[\n  M_x=Q_x-\\mu a_xH_x,\\qquad\n  M_y=Q_y-\\mu a_yH_y.\n\\]\n\n\\begin{task}[Verify shifted magnetic identities]\nStarting from \\eqref{eq:main-model}, verify\n\\begin{equation}\n\\begin{aligned}\n\\partial_tM_x\n&= a_x\\,\\partial_yE-\\frac{\\sy}{\\epsilon_0}M_x,\\\\\n\\partial_tM_y\n&= -a_y\\,\\partial_xE-\\frac{\\sx}{\\epsilon_0}M_y.\n\\end{aligned}\n\\label{eq:magnetic-shift}\n\\end{equation}\nThen test whether an energy written in terms of \\(H_x,H_y,M_x,M_y\\), rather than \\(H_x,H_y,Q_x,Q_y\\), has a cleaner dissipation structure.\n\\end{task}\n\n\\begin{remark}\nIf \\(\\sx,\\sy\\) are spatially variable, \\eqref{eq:magnetic-shift} itself does not produce \\(\\partial_t\\sigma\\) terms, because the coefficients are time-independent. These terms are likely to be one source of bounded-but-not-monotone estimates.\n\\end{remark}\n\n\\section{Electric PML Auxiliary Variables}\n\nThe variables \\(P_{z,1}\\) and \\(P_{z,2}\\) satisfy\n\\[\n  \\partial_tP_{z,1}=-\\frac{\\epsilon_\\infty}{\\epsilon_0}\\sx\\sy E,\\qquad\n  \\partial_tP_{z,2}=-\\frac{\\sx\\sy}{\\epsilon_0^2}P.\n\\]\nThey appear in the \\(E\\)-equation as \\(E(P_{z,1}+P_{z,2})\\).  This resembles the need for time-integrated or cross-term energies in PML analyses.\n\n\\begin{task}[Handle Pz1 and Pz2]\nTry the following routes:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n\\item define time-integrated variables\n\\[\n  R_1(t)=\\int_0^tP_{z,1}(s)\\dd s,\\qquad\n  R_2(t)=\\int_0^tP_{z,2}(s)\\dd s;\n\\]\n\\item add cross terms such as \\((E,P_{z,1})\\), \\((P,P_{z,2})\\), or weighted combinations;\n\\item freeze \\(\\sx,\\sy\\) as constants and solve the pointwise Lyapunov matrix problem for the electric subsystem \\((E,P,P_{z,1},P_{z,2})\\);\n\\item identify whether the corner factor \\(\\sx\\sy\\) is the essential obstruction.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\\end{task}\n\n\\section{Baffet-Type Energy Design Clue}\n\nBaffet--Grote--Imperiale--Kachanovska proved monotone energy decay for a second-order wave-equation PML with constant damping coefficients\\cite{baffetGroteImperialeKachanovska2019}. It explains why the v2 idea is\nclose to a useful construction in normal incidence, but it does not solve the\nfull 2D oblique problem: as soon as \\(k_y\\ne0\\), the exact stretched model\ncontains the ADE memory couplings displayed above.\n\n## Candidate 2: generalized CFS/ADE stretched-coordinate PML\n\nLet\n\\[\nS_i(s)=\\kappa_i+\\frac{\\sigma_i}{s+\\alpha_i},\n\\qquad\n\\kappa_i\\ge1,\\quad \\sigma_i\\ge0,\\quad \\alpha_i\\ge0.\n\\]\nThe repaired Laplace-domain equations are the same as Candidate 1, with these\n\\(S_i\\). No such\npositive memory theorem is claimed here for the full 2D Maxwell--Debye system.\n\nClassification: perfectly matched at the continuous planar-interface level;\nrecommended if long-time CFS behavior is needed; energy status is boundedness or\npassive-memory proof pending, not a completed monotone identity.\n\n## Candidate 3: MPML-type extra damping\n\nAn MPML-type repair adds damping in more than the normal coordinate direction.\nFor example, in an \\(x\\)-layer one may replace a scalar stretch by a multiaxial\nstretch depending also on tangential damping parameters.
